ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, two strips of paper, each with a width of 2, are overlapped at an angle of $30^\circ$. What is the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ formed by the overlapping part?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB \parallel CD$, \\
it follows that $\angle ABC = 30^\circ$, \\
Also, since the widths of both strips are 2, \\
it follows that $AB = 4$, \\
Similarly, it can be concluded that $AD = 4$, \\
Again, because $AB \parallel CD$ and $AD \parallel BC$, \\
it follows that quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a parallelogram, \\
Also, since $AB = AD = 4$, \\
it follows that quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rhombus, \\
Therefore, $S_{\text{rhombus}}ABCD = 4 \times 2 = \boxed{8}$.

Image description: In the figure there are two paper strips intersecting and overlapping, one roughly horizontal, and the other passing through it obliquely upward. The shaded overlapping part is labeled as quadrilateral ABCD, where AB and CD lie on the two parallel sides of the oblique paper strip, and AD and BC lie on the two parallel sides of the horizontal paper strip, so ABCD is a parallelogram. On the right side of the figure, the included angle of the two paper strips is marked as 30°, and the problem statement gives that the width of each paper strip is 2.
Reasoning: Because AB is parallel to CD, and AD is parallel to BC, quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram. The 30° in the figure is the angle between the direction of the oblique paper strip and the direction of the horizontal paper strip, so it can correspond to ∠ABC=30°. The width of the horizontal paper strip is 2, that is, the perpendicular distance between AD and BC is 2. When crossing this width along the oblique side AB, there is AB·sin30°=2, so AB=2/sin30°=4. Similarly, using the width of the oblique paper strip as 2, the adjacent side AD=2/sin30°=4 can be obtained. Therefore ABCD is a rhombus with side length 4. The area can be found by base times height: taking base AB=4, the corresponding height is exactly the paper strip width 2, so the area is 4×2=8.
